Hi Naomi / Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are our initial redlines to the MSA and the proposed order form. Two items we need help resolving before we can move to procurement sign-off:

1) Custody model for snapshots: we prefer a sealed-snapshot escrow model (third-party deposit) rather than operator access. We attached our escrow spec (escrow_spec_v2.docx). If Redwood can't accept third-party escrow deposit, we need a concrete alternative (timelines, witness access, verification steps).
2) KMS integration: for on-prem deployments we require that customer KMS-managed keys are used for model encryption at rest and that Redwood provide an HSM attestation workflow.

Please confirm whether those two items are acceptable and what the timeline looks like for redline review and a revised addendum. We are on a tight procurement window — ideally signed before the end of Sep.

--- Message 2 ---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — initial redlines and custody question

Luca — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. High level reply here, we'll follow with a redline-ready draft by Monday 13 Sep:

- Escrow / sealed snapshot: Redwood does support a witnessable snapshot deposit workflow for select private deployments. We typically offer two patterns:
  * Operator-witnessed deposit (Redwood operator produces snapshot in the customer environment and the snapshot hash + sealed envelope is deposited with a third party), or
  * Customer-first sealed deposit (customer generates snapshot and can deposit directly with a neutral escrow agent).

  We can accept the customer-first sealed deposit approach if CarePath is comfortable with the chain-of-custody steps in your spec. If you want Redwood to be able to validate or witness the deposit we will need specific windows and a limited access plan (see below).

- KMS / HSM: we support customer-managed keys via remote KMS integrations for VPC deployments (KMS-initiated envelope keys). For on-prem we support local HSM/KMS integration but need to validate the key wrapping approach. Alex to confirm technical constraints for the image and snapshot encryption path.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alex: can you confirm the technical feasibility and a short note on any image/snapshot constraints by EOD Fri 10 Sep?
2) Legal (David): can you draft a short MSA addendum that captures both the custody options and the KMS attestation clause? Aim: one page of binding language + defined exhibits (witness flow or escrow exhibit).
3) Luca / CarePath: confirm which custody pattern you prefer (customer-first sealed deposit OR Redwood-witnessed) and whether you have a preferred escrow vendor (you mentioned TrustEscrow in the doc).

I will schedule a 30-min sync for Mon 13 Sep to walk the redline — sending calendar invite now.

Thanks — Naomi
Head of Customer Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 ---

Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — initial redlines and custody question

Quick technical note on the KMS and snapshot path:

- For VPC-hosted private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/CloudHSM, GCP KMS) using envelope encryption. The runtime image will be built with keys wrapped; snapshots (storage slices) are encrypted with customer-managed envelope keys.
- For on-prem installs, the supported patterns are:
  1) Customer-managed HSM on-site: Redwood runtime configured to use local HSM for key wrapping; snapshot files remain encrypted with keys that never leave customer KMS.
  2) Redwood-managed key-wrapping (only with customer explicit provision in order form): Redwood will use an HSM managed by the customer or a mutually agreed provider; we will provide key usage logs and an attestation report.

Constraints / ask: if CarePath wants Redwood to perform a witness deposit (operator involvement), we need a 2–4 hour scheduled window to produce the snapshot and perform the validation steps; the operator will not extract keys — only the snapshot hash and metadata for escrow. If you want continuous witness capability (on-demand), we need a slightly different service agreement and a small ops fee.

I'll prepare a short tech exhibit for the addendum and upload to the shared doc.

— Alex
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — initial redlines and custody question

Luca / CarePath team — attaching an MSA addendum draft and an escrow exhibit that follow the customer-first sealed deposit model but also preserve Redwood the right to witness under a narrowly scoped process. Key points:

- License scope: clarified that model runtime binaries are licensed to customer for the duration of the order form and limited to the deployed environment(s) listed in Exhibit A; customer may not redistribute.
- Custody: customer may deposit sealed snapshot with an agreed escrow agent (TrustEscrow). Redwood agrees to provide a cryptographic hash and a signed metadata manifest upon request to validate a deposit, but Redwood will not be required to store or hold operational snapshots except for purpose-built forensic tests agreed in advance.
- Attestation: Redwood will provide an annual HSM attestation report for dedicated/private deployments where Redwood manages any portion of key wrapping. For on-prem fully customer-managed KMS, Redwood will accept customer-supplied attestation and may request a technical validation session.

Action items:
1) CarePath to confirm preferred custody model and whether TrustEscrow is acceptable.
2) CarePath legal to review attached addendum and propose redlines.
3) Naomi / Alex / I will incorporate any technical exhibits and finalize the addendum for signature — target: 2027-09-20.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Addendum_Custody_20270913.docx, Escrow_Exhibit_Redwood_v1.pdf

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
